newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican judge frees two jailed priests.
newsitem.headline: Mexican judge frees two jailed priests.

text.p: A Mexican judge on Thursday freed two Jesuit priests who Mexico's Roman Catholic church said had been falsely arrested on trumped-up murder charges, officials said.

Judge Fausto Blas, a district judge in the capital of the troubled southern state of Chiapas, ruled there was not enough evidence to jail the two priests and two local Indian leaders on charges they led a deadly ambush last week on police.

The priests, Geronimo Lopez and Gonzalo Rosas, and Indian leaders Ramon Parcero and Francisco Gonzalez were arrested last Saturday for allegedly killing two policemen and injuring five in a land dispute.
Their case was taken up by human rights groups and the church, which said the priests were attending a religious conference in a different city at the time of the ambush.
State officials accused the four men of ambushing police after they had dislodged Indian peasants from land the farmers had illegally seized near the tourist city of Palenque.
The two Indians said the killings occurred when police, backed by helicopters, started shooting at the peasants, who fired back.
Local church officials said the arrests were a crackdown by local politicians angered by the church's work with peasants in the turbulent state, where a Mayan rebellion has simmered since 1994.
